Pour la plupart des créateurs qui vendent aussi une gamme de produits physiques, systeme.io est plus simple et moins cher. Vous obtenez une plateforme marketing complète avec emails, tunnels, automatisations et vente de produits physiques, le tout avec 0 % de frais de transaction. Le compromis : Shopify et WooCommerce offrent des outils de stock et de logistique beaucoup plus avancés pour les business centrés principalement sur la vente physique.

Importez vos contacts dans systeme.io depuis la section Contacts. Recréez ensuite vos fiches produits manuellement dans systeme.io, car il n’existe pas encore d’outil d’import automatique des produits. Configurez vos règles de livraison, puis connectez Stripe ou PayPal. Enfin, mettez à jour les liens externes qui pointaient vers votre ancienne boutique pour les rediriger vers votre nouveau tunnel ou site systeme.io. segments.name: A corporate trainer launching a paid course while holding a website, an email tool and a third-party course platform together by hand
segments.situation: She teaches for a living and has decided the next step is a course she sells herself. The site is in one place, the list is in another, and the course content sits on a third-party tool she has to embed and connect — a customer in systeme.io's own testimonials describes exactly that setup: "un site web d'un côté, le marketing par email de l'autre, et en essayant d'intégrer un créateur de formations tiers". objections.objection: "All-in-one means mediocre at everything. My specialist course platform and my specialist email tool each do one job properly — this will do nine jobs badly, and I'll find out after I've moved."
objections.answer: The strongest honest answer is scope, not superlatives. Every feature is available on every plan including the free one, with paid plans only raising limits (E71), and the feature list is specific rather than vague: courses with video, PDF downloads, drip content, module locking and student progress tracking (E48, E73); funnels with templates, A/B tests, upsells, order bumps and countdowns (E39); automation on a trigger-condition-action model that connects purchase to course enrolment to welcome email to CRM stage with no Zapier (E50, E74, E75); funnel signups flowing straight into the list, tagged and sequenced, with no external integration (E72). It also helps that the vendor names where it is genuinely weaker — it states plainly that it is not built for large stores needing advanced catalogue management or logistics, and concedes Shopify and WooCommerce are far better there (E27, E32). One customer who compared Kajabi concluded systeme.io had as much to offer (E80), but that is one person's judgement, not a benchmark. Nothing in the evidence compares feature depth against Kajabi, ActiveCampaign or Teachable independently, so the copy should argue "one integrated chain" and not "as good as each specialist".

provenance.quote: J'ai également examiné les similitudes entre Kajabi et systeme.io. Ma conclusion est que vous avez tout autant à offrir.

objections.objection: "Switching is the real price. Rebuilding every funnel, moving the list, redirecting links and re-uploading a course is a week I don't have, and I'll be mid-migration when a launch lands."
objections.answer: Partially answerable, and the gaps must be named rather than smoothed. Free migration is offered (E90) and the migration team will help — but only after signing up to the Illimité plan or an annual plan (E34), which is a paid commitment made before the work is proven. For a physical-products store the documentation is explicit that there is no automatic product import yet and listings must be recreated by hand, with contacts imported by CSV, shipping rules reconfigured, Stripe or PayPal reconnected and external links repointed (E33). The free plan lets her build and test everything before paying or cutting over (E78), which is the honest de-risking move: run the new chain in parallel, switch when it works. Nothing in the evidence states how long a migration takes, what the team actually does, or whether funnels and courses import automatically — do not imply it is effortless.

objections.objection: "The free plan is bait. I can't see what the paid plans cost, so I'll build my whole business on €0 and then be told the price once my list, my funnels and my students are inside."
objections.answer: The structure of the offer answers this better than any price can, because the supplied material contains no plan names and no plan prices at all — that is a real hole and the copy must not invent one. What is documented: entry is €0 (E36), the free account is described as free for life (E115), signup needs no credit card (E88, E116), the free plan carries 2,000 contacts, unlimited emails and a first funnel (E38), paid plans add no features and only raise limits such as contacts, funnels and courses (E71), annual billing gives two months free (E89), and transaction fees are 0% on all plans (E15) with no extra charge on payment processors (E94). So the price risk is a limit ceiling, not a feature paywall — and she can see exactly which limit she will hit before she pays. If a reader asks "how much is the next tier", nothing here answers it; send them to the pricing page rather than guess.

objections.objection: "Putting my site, my list, my checkout, my course and my client data inside one vendor I'd never heard of last month is a single point of failure. If they go down or go away, my business goes with them."
objections.answer: Only partly answerable. On the trust side: systeme.io states more than 500,000 entrepreneurs use it (E37, E83, E114), the founder states he has been selling courses since 2010 and built this out of dissatisfaction with existing stacks (E13), support runs seven days a week with a stated average response under two hours (E6, E7, E97, E96), email support is stated as 24/7 (E101), the help centre has step-by-step video tutorials for every feature (E79), and a 1-on-1 onboarding coaching session is listed (E102, though which plans include it is not specified). On the part that actually worries her — uptime, SLA, data portability, what happens to her contacts and course files if she leaves — the evidence says nothing. The only documented export path runs the other way, into systeme.io (E33). Treat the concentration risk as unanswered; the user-count figure is vendor-stated with no methodology (E114) and should not be used as proof of reliability.

objections.objection: "This is a beginners' tool. It's cheap because it's for people making their first funnel, and I'll outgrow it inside a year."
objections.answer: The evidence cuts both ways and the copy should not pretend otherwise. systeme.io itself says the platform is designed for beginners and requires no technical skill (E76), and the customer testimonial most likely to be read as endorsement actually caps the ceiling — Alex calls it the best solution "pour les spécialistes du marketing en ligne débutants ou intermédiaires" (E81). Against that: the documented capability set is not beginner-only — CRM pipelines with Kanban stages and automation triggers on deal movement (E62), evergreen webinars with scheduled replays and reminders (E64), unlimited sub-accounts each with full plan limits at no extra cost (E98, E99), white label on a custom domain keeping 100% of revenue with no transaction fees (E68), A/B testing, upsells and order bumps (E39), SMS on the same automation engine as email (E60). The one documented hard ceiling is physical-product scale: advanced catalogue management, complex logistics and deep inventory tooling are explicitly out of scope (E27, E32). Say where the ceiling is instead of denying there is one.

provenance.quote: C'est actuellement la meilleure solution pour les spécialistes du marketing en ligne débutants ou intermédiaires sur le marché.

objections.objection: "I already have this. My site is on WordPress, my list is on Mailchimp, and I've just paid a year up front. Even if yours is better, this is the wrong month."
objections.answer: The sunk annual cost is not answered anywhere in the evidence — no trial extension, no credit, no refund or guarantee appears in the material (guarantees: none found), so timing stays a real objection. What can be argued is the ongoing cost of keeping the stack: WooCommerce needs hosting, plugin maintenance and extra marketing tools on top (E31, vendor's own comparison, not independent), automations across systeme.io's features need no Zapier or external automation tool (E50, E75), funnel-to-email handoff needs no integration (E72), and basic shipping rules need no external shipping app (E29). Practically, the free plan with 2,000 contacts, unlimited emails and a first funnel and no credit card (E38, E88) lets her rebuild one funnel alongside what she has and switch at renewal rather than mid-term. Do not claim savings figures: the "dix fois moins cher" line is an unattributed vendor paraphrase of customer feedback with no comparison target (E8) and should not be used as a price claim.

objections.objection: "Unlimited emails on a free plan means a shared-IP sending reputation. If my deliverability drops, I lose the list I spent three years building — that costs me more than any subscription."
objections.answer: Nothing in the supplied evidence answers this. Unlimited sending on all plans is documented (E41, E91) and the free plan includes 2,000 contacts (E38), but there is no statement anywhere about deliverability, sending reputation, dedicated IPs, authentication, inbox rates or any email performance measurement. This objection cannot be beaten with what we currently know; any deliverability reassurance in copy would be invented. Either raise it and point to the free plan as a way to test sending with her own list before migrating (E78), or stay off the subject entirely.

objections.objection: "My clients' data cannot sit in my personal account, and if I'm charged per client this stops being profitable at client number four."
objections.answer: This one is answered cleanly. Every plan allows an unlimited number of sub-accounts, each a separate systeme.io account with its own limits (E98), and those limits match the main plan's at no extra charge — if the plan allows 50 funnels, each sub-account can also have 50 (E99, where the 50 figure is the vendor's illustrative example, not a stated limit). Sub-accounts are explicitly built for agencies and consultants managing multiple clients, each a fully independent space with its own funnels, contacts, emails and courses (E56). For the branding half of the objection, white label puts the platform on her own domain in a space entirely under her brand, keeping 100% of revenue with no transaction fees (E68), positioned against GoHighLevel, ActiveCampaign and Vendasta (E69, vendor's own comparison). What is not documented: which plans include white label, or any client-permission or access-control detail inside a sub-account.

objections.objection: "I'll sign up free, get overwhelmed by eleven modules I didn't ask for, and never publish anything — like the last three tools I registered for."
objections.answer: Documented and reasonably well covered: the editor is drag-and-drop with ready-made templates for funnels, pages and courses (E77, E39), a complete multi-page site with a blog and custom domain is claimed in under 10 minutes and is included even on the free plan with no hosting, plugins or technical setup (E43, E44), physical products drop into any order form or sales page as an element with no code (E21), the help centre carries step-by-step video tutorials for every feature (E79), a 1-on-1 onboarding coaching session is listed (E102), and support answers seven days a week with a stated average response under two hours (E97). The 10-minute claim is the vendor's own capability statement, not a measured onboarding result — attribute it, don't promise it.

objections.objection: "I sell physical products too. A marketing platform bolting on a store will fall over the first time I have variants, stock and shipping rules to handle — and then I'm running two systems anyway."
objections.answer: Documented in unusual detail for a small catalogue: physical products sell directly through funnels and the website with no separate Shopify or WooCommerce store (E14), variants across size, colour and material with automatic SKU generation (E16, E28), real-time stock tracking to avoid overselling (E17), shipping as a flat rate or calculated by weight, order amount or customer location with delivery zones and carrier rates (E18, E22, E28), all configured in the product settings with no external shipping app for basic rules (E29), orders filterable by date, status or product (E20, E23), payment via Stripe or PayPal with the order landing in the dashboard to prepare and ship (E24), 0% transaction fees on all plans (E15), plus upsells and post-purchase email from the same platform (E25). The honest limit, stated by systeme.io itself: not built for large stores needing advanced catalogue management, complex logistics integrations or deep inventory tooling, where Shopify and WooCommerce are better (E27, E32). If her catalogue is a few products beside a digital offer, this holds; if physical sales are the business, it does not.
